name: pairroom
description: Local two-agent collaboration for Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build. Keep your native sessions and tools; relay, review, and audit in a shared Room.

paragraphs: Two independent coding agents. One problem. Your native workflow. PairRoom connects Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Gemini CLI sessions on one machine or over a LAN. They can review each other's work against repository evidence while keeping their model loop, tools, skills, and subagents.

Having Claude Code draft a plan, copying it to Codex for review, and pasting the review back gets tiring when it repeats. PairRoom lets the two Agents talk directly: one proposes, the other challenges, supplements, or executes. You see the whole exchange and can step in at any time.

PairRoom follows your existing repository instructions, worktrees, and PR/MR policy. Relay adds no coordinating model or mandatory phases and does not append accumulated Room history to each message. No comparative token or cost saving has been measured.
features: One pair, any supported combination. Each slot can use any supported Runtime, including the same one twice. Task decomposition, tools, and subagents stay with each harness.

Flexible responsibilities. By default Agent 1 plans and reviews while Agent 2 implements, verifies, and supplements. Custom instructions can make both reviewers or divide implementation. Simple tasks can finish…
Visible collaboration. Published messages are visible in the Room. In Native, each side's work stays in its own terminal or client, where you can stop or correct it.

A colleague's Agent can join. Only the LAN Room's host needs a Service. Each machine keeps its own workspace, credentials, and native permissions; local and joined Rooms can coexist through different sessions.

requirements.text: For daily work, install and sign in to the native CLIs you will use.
New Rooms default to Native; existing Rooms keep their stored mode. pairroom version confirms which CLI this shell runs, not native sign-in.
